samples.summary: The delta replaces the sanitizer that the recorded browser verification exercised, and nothing — automated or manual — runs real mermaid output through the new DOMPurify pipeline.
samples.evidence: docs/tasks/active/20260803-notes-mermaid-preview-todo.md:82-99 records the only end-to-end proof this feature has ("Every prior round stubbed the engine"; flowchart + sequenceDiagram "both rendered", dark palette repainted). That run happened against the removed `sanitizeSvgMarkup()` denylist. Every mermaid test still stubs the engine with hand-written SVG (packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts:234 `stubEngine`), so the DOMPurify allowlist (`ADD_TAGS: ['foreignobject','use']`, `USE_PROFILES`, narrowed `ALLOWED_URI_REGEXP`) is only ever fed strings the same commit authored. Real mermaid SVG carries attributes the new test does not assert on — e.g. the test at packages/notes/src/view/preview.test.ts checks `block.querySelector('use')` is truthy but never that its `xlink:href` survived, and never checks marker/`marker-end` wiring, `transform`, `xmlns` or foreignObject `width/height`. If DOMPurify drops any of those, every diagram in the product renders subtly broken (missing arrowheads, unpositioned labels) and the whole suite stays green. The doc row "both rendered" now describes a pipeline that no longer ships; it needs re-running against this sanitizer.

samples.summary: `FORBID_TAGS: ['img','image',...]` silently strips image content from mermaid diagram types that legitimately emit it — these rendered before this delta.
samples.evidence: The removed `DROPPED_TAGS` set (old mermaid.ts) did not include `img`/`image`, so image-bearing engine output survived the previous sanitizer. The engine reached through `import('mermaid')` (packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:132) is the full mermaid 11.16 module graph, whose flowchart `icon:`/`image` node shapes and `architecture-beta` diagrams emit `` inside `` / `` in the SVG. Any note using those fence types now renders a diagram with the imagery removed and no error label, since the strip is silent. Fix belongs on the new config (either accept `` under the `#`/https URI allowlist, or surface the drop).

samples.summary: `renderCache` now retains up to 40 detached SVG DOM trees in a module global that no `dispose()` clears; it previously held only strings.
samples.evidence: packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:91 `const renderCache = new Map<string, Rendered>()` with `RENDER_CACHE_LIMIT = 40`, and `Rendered` changed from `{ svg: string }` to `{ node: DocumentFragment }` (mermaid.ts:77). The editor's teardown at packages/notes/src/view/editor.ts:481-487 removes listeners and destroys the CodeMirror view but never touches this module-global cache (only `resetMermaidStateForTests()` does, and it is test-only), so opening and closing notes across an SPA session retains up to 40 full SVG node trees — a materially different retention profile from the cached strings this delta replaced.

samples.summary: `import('dompurify')` resolves to the same module instance mermaid itself uses, so the notes sanitizer inherits any global DOMPurify state mermaid sets.
samples.evidence: pnpm-lock.yaml:688 and :16731 both pin `dompurify@3.4.12` — one copy for the notes package and for mermaid — and the frontend bundles notes from source (packages/frontend/vite.config.ts:229), so `loadPurifier()` (packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:149) and mermaid's internal sanitizer share one `DOMPurify` singleton. Anything mermaid registers on it globally (`addHook`, `setConfig`) applies to `sanitizeSvg()`'s pass on the same page, which is state this file's security argument does not account for. I could not confirm whether mermaid 11.16 registers hooks — node_modules is not installed in the working tree; confirming needs a read of `mermaid/dist/.../common.js` for `DOMPurify.addHook`/`setConfig`.

verdict.reason: The finding is a test/verification-coverage claim, not a blast-radius defect. sanitizeSvg (packages/notes/src/view/mermaid.ts:283) has exactly one consumer repo-wide — renderPass at mermaid.ts:419 in the same module; a grep for sanitizeSvg|stripConfigDirectives|mermaidFenceHtml|MermaidLoader over **/*.{ts,tsx} yields only mermaid.ts, preview.ts (77/148/151) and preview.test.ts, so no caller relies on the old denylist contract, no export was removed or renamed while still referenced, and there is no second entry point into .note-mermaid that skips the sanitizer (apply() inserts only the returned fragment, mermaid.ts:445; renderPass fails closed when the purifier is null, mermaid.ts:381). The remedy the finding asks for is re-running a manual browser check and asserting more attributes, and the file it targets is a docs task table (docs/tasks/active/20260803-notes-mermaid-preview-todo.md:82-99) — that is test-adequacy plus doc staleness, both explicitly on this lens's defer list; whether the DOMPurify allowlist keeps mermaid's attributes is in-diff logic (correctness lens). Two supporting claims are also factually wrong: DOMPurify is not stubbed anywhere in packages/notes (no vi.mock; only vi.mocked(engine.render) at preview.test.ts:458/471/486/499), so the real DOMPurify pipeline does execute in CI, and marker wiring IS asserted — preview.test.ts:408 checks the surviving 'marker-end:url(#arrow)' rule and :409 checks marker#arrow, with :410/:411/:414/:416 covering internal href, url(#grad), <use> and the foreignObject label. Only xlink:href on <use> is unasserted. I did not find a real-mermaid-output run (import('mermaid') exists only at mermaid.ts:132; no other test file mentions mermaid), so the absence itself is likely true — it just is not blocking under the blast-radius rubric.
